# Licensing and provenance

Current UPG functionality uses native implementations. These notices retain
historical attribution and pinned design references, not active dependencies.
They must not be interpreted as endorsement or independent efficacy evidence.

`offline-learning-MIT.txt` and `offline-learning-history.json` preserve the
original MIT notice and file provenance for the retired learning dependency.
Its full source remains recoverable from Git at
`929906bd29ceb581d55fcaf9ebb28fd2a22eba0d`; the working copy was also archived
with byte-verified source backups before retirement. Historical audit and
protocol identifiers have not been rewritten.

`project-recovery-MIT.txt` preserves the license of the reviewed design reference
at commit `cab634bd855fc287f6e420c1f36fd1a6b9245960`.
`project-recovery-design.json` identifies the inspected files. UPG implements
task-scoped fact recovery in its existing state/planner structures; it does not
copy or load that package's routing, tools, scripts or case database.

UPG intentionally keeps file fixity separate from empirical validity, preserves
original evidence and unknown intent, and never grants a finding validated
status merely because an evidence file exists.

`focused-governance.json` records selectively adapted Caveman and Ponytail instructions, pinned revisions, file identities and exclusions. Their notices in `governance-src/notices/` also ship in the generated LICENSE. No upstream runtime or hooks are installed.
